bio: I started out making maps. For thirteen years at Ambo University in Ethiopia I taught GIS and remote sensing, studied how changing land use was reshaping watersheds and soils, and served as Head of the Department of Land Administration and Surveying and then Dean of the School of Natural Resources.

In 2023 I came to the University of Florida to work on a more direct question: how do we know whether a soil is healthy, given where it is and how it is farmed? In the Sustainable Tropical Soil Management Lab, advised by Dr. Márcio R. Nunes, I build soil health benchmarks and soil organic carbon maps that respect local context, and turn them into tools such as gSHAPE.

I care about research that a land manager can use, students who leave a lab able to do the work themselves, and data that travels from Ethiopia to Brazil to Florida. I live in Gainesville with my family.
